summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, pancreas transplant, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and recent CABG was admitted from rehabilitation due to fatigue and anemia with a hematocrit of 25. She had guaiac-positive stool but no active bleeding, and her anemia was attributed to chronic kidney disease. She received two units of packed red blood cells with improvement in hemoglobin to 9.6 g/dL. Chronic diarrhea was evaluated and found to be non-infectious, with C. difficile testing negative; management included increasing pancreatic enzyme replacement and starting loperamide. She completed a course of fluconazole for candidal esophagitis and was transitioned to suppressive therapy. Her peritoneal dialysis continued without complications, and her immunosuppressive regimen was maintained. Vancomycin dosing was adjusted based on trough levels for ongoing cellulitis. She remained stable, with no signs of infection or cardiac issues, and was discharged to extended care with follow-up plans and medication adjustments.
